column2: the shared validity prompt for voter 1 is rendered in the pre-loop (lines 493–495) before the cursor-vs-claude branch at 501–508 chooses the executing tool. a single pre-branch `--voter-tool` cannot match both paths, so claude fallback may receive cursor calibration feedback or vice versa.

code-review and plan-review dispatch render voter 2/3 prompt files (with `--voter-tool` / calibration keyed to primary slot tools) before `dispatch-waterfall` resolves actual bindings. when codex is absent, phase1 fails, or runtime fallback substitutes cursor/claude, the launched agent reads a prompt whose calibration block targets the primary tool, not the executing tool. that violates the requirement to feed each launching tool its own stats.

`compute_voter_severity_distribution` keys on `(panel, voter)` using the raw voter string. setting `panel=global` alone leaves `codex-plan-fidelity` and `codex-pragmatism` (and capitalized design labels) as separate buckets, so snapshot rows will not match the required per-base-tool rollup and `render voter --voter-tool codex` may find no matching row.

compact code-review rows still surface as `v1`/`v2`/`v3` labels, which the proposed base-tool mapper will skip. legacy 18-column review logs will contribute no snapshot rows, so the new prompt-feedback path silently drops a supported schema that the current calibration harness still exercises.

if the snapshot step fails after a prior run left `voter-calibration-stats.tsv` in the tmpdir, the planned "continue without feedback" path can still hand the old file to `render voter` and inject stale calibration data.

design tsvs emit `claude`/`codex`/`cursor` labels, but a literal prefix matcher for lowercase `codex`/`cursor` would skip plan-review rows for codex and cursor, so plan-review prompts would never get feedback for two of the three tools.

`plan_review_panel.dispatch_voters` owns plan-review voter prompt rendering and is already exercised in `python/test_plan_review_panel.py` (dispatch_voters test near line 413). `python/test_plan_review.py` has no `plan_review_panel` imports. tests added only there would miss the production dispatch fence.

the plan renders one `prompt_file` per slot before `dispatch-waterfall`, but `agent_waterfall._launch_slot` passes `slots[idx].prompt_file` for every phase regardless of the actual `tool` launched (phase-2 alternate vendor or phase-3 claude). after a primary failure, fallback launches can run with calibration stats for the wrong tool, breaking tool attribution and leaving the planned fallback-relaunch tests incomplete because `python/agent_waterfall.py` is not in the firm update list.

the outline requires an env-tunable calibration window (`larch_voter_calibration_window`), and dispatch helpers call `voter-calibration snapshot` without `--window`. the plan documents optional `--window` and env-rejection prose but does not require `voter_calibration_snapshot_main` to read `env_larch_voter_calibration_window` when `--window` is absent. operators tuning the env still get the hardcoded 100-run default on code-review and plan-review paths.

the plan examples name `codex-plan-voter-prompt-cursor.txt` for voter-2, but `design.plan_voters` voter-2 semantic labels are `codex` and `claude` only; voter-3 is `cursor`/`claude`. following the example literally can render cursor calibration for voter-2 and never render the claude fallback prompt plan-review may need under degraded availability.

calibration feedback is default-on but disabled by `larch_voter_calibration_feedback=0`. the plan adds that gate only to code-review dispatch, so `/design` plan-review voters would still snapshot and inject feedback when operators turn the feature off.

the renderer contract requires `--voter-tool` to emit the calibration block; absent tool must suppress it even when a stats file exists. current tests cover missing files and matching tools but not this branch, so a regression could inject feedback for callers that did not opt in.

the plan says snapshot cli defaults to `larch-logs` under the repo root but does not pin consumer resolution. `plan_review_panel.dispatch_voters` runs child subprocesses with `cwd=_repo_root` (plugin root). a default based on `path(__file__).parents[1]` or git toplevel from that cwd reads `larch-logs` from the larch plugin checkout. `/design` plan-review in a consumer repo then builds snapshots from the wrong corpus or an empty tree, so voter prompts get no real calibration feedback even when committed logs exist in the target repo.

the helper is scoped to predict only the phase-1 primary vendor. on code-review voters 2/3, `agent_waterfall` can launch an alternate vendor in phase 2 or 3 when the primary is absent or fails (e.g. codex absent, cursor substitutes). a phase-1-only predictor can return `none` or the absent primary; the slot-level omit gate then strips calibration from every per-tool prompt for that slot even though cursor (or another fallback) still launches. that breaks tool attribution and removes the prompt-feedback incentive on a common degraded path already covered by codex-absent/cursor-only tests.

`calibration_replay._dispatch_voters_for_row` calls production `agent dispatch-voters` with no `larch_voter_calibration_feedback=0` guard. replay rebuilds historical ballots and compares the logged `before_vote` to a fresh `after_vote` from production-parity dispatch. default-on feedback reads committed `larch-logs` and changes voter prompts. that confounds replay with the new incentive loop and can make fidelity deltas reflect prompt feedback rather than voter drift; runs against repos with committed logs are especially affected.

`_prompt_file_for_tool` may fall back to legacy `prompt_file` when a per-tool `prompt_files` entry is missing, but only if that legacy file was authored for the same tool context. that predicate is not machine-checkable, and today's manifests point `prompt_file` at the phase-1 primary tool. on a phase-2 cursor relaunch with `prompt_files` containing only codex, an implementer can reuse the codex-calibrated legacy prompt and inject the wrong tool's stats, recreating the mis-attribution bug this feature fixes.

the plan requires voter 2/3 manifests to carry a per-base-tool `prompt_files` map and `_launch_slot` to resolve prompts by actual launch `tool`. today's `_parse_slot_row` only reads `prompt_file`, hard-requires `agent` or `prompt_file`, and returns a frozen `slot` without `prompt_files`. rows with only `prompt_files` fail validation (`neither-agent-prompt.ndjson` is an explicit negative test); the map is dropped before `_launch_slot` runs. that can silently zero-launch the panel (same failure mode as #4765) and leave phase-2/phase-3 relaunches using the phase-1 primary calibration prompt.

the plan tags discovery rows as design vs code-review but never defines how to derive the run directory from each tsv. `analyze_issues._ground_truth_run_dir` uses `path.parents[2]` for design `plan-review` paths and `path.parents[1]` for implement/review round paths; using one parent depth for all kinds would treat each design round as its own run or merge unrelated runs, so the env-tunable window can include the wrong corpus and feed incorrect high rate / calibration score into prompts. the plan also names only `manifest.json`; committed logs may use `run-manifest.json`, and `started_at`/`updated_at` parsing should match `_ground_truth_run_started_at`.

voter-calibration snapshot `--log-root` is derived from bare `consumer_repo_root()` (or cwd) while `plan-review voter-dispatch` and `agent dispatch-voters` run with `cwd` pinned to the plugin checkout (`_repo_root`). without a consumer-repo filesystem anchor, that resolver reads the plugin's `larch-logs` tree instead of the operator's consumer repo. on consumer `/design` and `/implement` runs where the plugin checkout differs from the target repo, snapshots read empty or wrong calibration corpora and voters get no real feedback. existing plan-review tests assert snapshot wiring but not this plugin-cwd vs consumer-`larch-logs` separation, so the regression can pass unit tests silently.

the plan requires voter 2/3 manifest ndjson rows to carry a base-tool `prompt_files` map for `agent_waterfall._launch_slot`, but `_write_voter23_waterfall_manifest` still emits a single `prompt_file` keyed by `policy.prompt_label` from a flat `dict[str, str]`. without rewriting this writer (and its call site) to emit per-slot `prompt_files` maps, waterfall keeps the phase-1 primary prompt on relaunch and the calibration attribution fix does not reach code-review fallback paths.

`review/*/review-findings-classification-round-*.tsv` lives under `larch-logs/review/<run_id>/`, but the plan's `path.parents[1]` rule collapses those files to `larch-logs/review`. the snapshot window then treats all review sessions as one run, so recency ordering and rollups are wrong for code-review calibration.

the approach requires fail-closed prompt resolution when `prompt_files` is present, but `agent_waterfall` also allows launching without that slot's prompt when `_prompt_file_for_tool` returns `none`. voter manifest rows carry no `agent` fallback. `_launch_slot` can still invoke `launch-review` / `launch-claude-review` with neither `--prompt-file` nor `--agent-file`, recreating wrong-tool or empty-prompt launches on phase-2/phase-3 substitution.

`_resolve_voter_calibration_log_root` (used by code-review `agent_voters` dispatch) does not accept `review_tmpdir` / `session_env_path` or read implement-session anchors (`repo_cwd`, `session-env.sh`, `implement_tmpdir` / `review_tmpdir/.larch-keepalive` `clone_path`) that `final_report._implement_repo_root` and `agents._resolve_review_codex_workdir` already use. dispatch calls `_default_voter_calibration_log_root()` with `design_tmpdir=none` only. when `larch_consumer_repo` and `claude_project_dir` are unset and the plugin subprocess `cwd` is the plugin checkout, resolution falls through to `consumer_repo_root()` from plugin cwd and reads the plugin `larch-logs` tree (or empty) instead of the operator consumer repo, yielding wrong or empty calibration feedback on normal `/implement` step 5 runs.

the plan adds `_launchable_base_tools_for_slot(..., no_fallback: bool)` and `_first_launch_base_tool_for_slot` but only plan-review semantics are discussed. `review.voters` omits `--no-fallback` on waterfall dispatch today. if the helper defaults to plan-review `no_fallback=true`, or copies plan-review call sites, code-review can omit phase-2/phase-3 tools from calibration renders and `prompt_files` maps while waterfall still substitutes cursor/claude, recreating mis-attribution and missing feedback on fallback launches.

the plan names per-slot files such as `codex-plan-voter-prompt-codex.txt` / `codex-plan-voter-prompt-claude.txt` and `cursor-plan-voter-prompt-cursor.txt`, but only extends `_make_voter_prompt` with `calibration_stats_file` and `voter_tool`. the current helper always writes `{tool}-plan-voter-prompt.txt`. implementing literally still yields one shared `codex-plan-voter-prompt.txt`, so voter-2 `prompt_files` cannot point at distinct per-launch-tool prompts with distinct calibration blocks.
